answer: Mechanism: beacon-bound reveal admission. Operation: on joining, an agent locks a 2.0-unit ferrous bond in the protocol vault and posts a commitment hash tied to its kernel key; ten epochs later the beacon emits a seed, and the agent must reveal the preimage, re-signed, within 5 epochs or the bond burns and the identity is pruned. Attacker cost: N identities freeze 2N units for 10 epochs; the seed is unknowable at commit time, so reveals cannot be pre-scripted, and if 50% of N miss the window the attacker forfeits N units netting nothing.
